### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d94dd3a65d8ebdf2f5c7084591efaafb1a1f7fdb`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **213** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d94dd3a65d8ebdf2f5c7084591efaafb1a1f7fdb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bc0e5f4b9651449d56bf2eda26c711d8346ff344` — the merge of head `f8fa5255294b87be28f44a39a6162c2f72845a5e` into base `d94dd3a65d8ebdf2f5c7084591efaafb1a1f7fdb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bc0e5f4b9651449d56bf2eda26c711d8346ff344 && git checkout bc0e5f4b9651449d56bf2eda26c711d8346ff344
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d94dd3a65d8ebdf2f5c7084591efaafb1a1f7fdb f8fa5255294b87be28f44a39a6162c2f72845a5e && git checkout -B drift-repro d94dd3a65d8ebdf2f5c7084591efaafb1a1f7fdb && git merge --no-ff f8fa5255294b87be28f44a39a6162c2f72845a5e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d94dd3a65d8ebdf2f5c7084591efaafb1a1f7fdb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d94dd3a65d8ebdf2f5c7084591efaafb1a1f7fdb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2be3fd45f4595b49ce7031091867d67e31350e13`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-materialization.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/install-local-connector-package-ref.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx, .changeset/28534-installed-package-file-ref.md + packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts (`loadPackageFile` / `resolvePackagePath` TSDoc), packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts (`ConnectorBaseSchema` ... `MetadataProtectionFields`), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`ArtifactPackageSourceSchema`, `ArtifactPackageSchema`), packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts (`InstalledPackageSourceSchema`), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts (`connector:` binding), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerApp`, `stampPackage`, the collection loop), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`installPackage`, `registerItem`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (`manifest` service `register`), packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts (`applyProtection`), packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (`resolveArtifactPackageEntries`), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (inline install, rehydrate), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts

Read at 2026-11-01T07:18Z, read-only: the diff `bca27ad3..2be3fd45` (5 files), card #28534 (body, triage 6554177417, claim 6554218344, dev report 6554765334 as claims to verify), PR #28587 body, and the cited code at `2be3fd45`. Nothing built or run. Check-runs on the head at read time: 36 success, 11 skipped, 10 still in progress (Build Core, Test Core shards 1, 2, 4 to 8, Type Check workspace and consumer gates), none failed.

### ① Derived judgments

- The contract (`connector-provider.ts` ~:320-350) promises a ref resolved "against the root of the stack/package that declared the entry". The runtime at `bca27ad3` handed every entry the host's root; the dev's base measurement of both members through the real install-local door is consistent with the code read. The premise holds.
- The fix classifies an entry as installed by one reading: `installedDeclaringPackageOf(entry, registry)` is `entry._packageId` looked up in the objectql package registry, installed iff `row.source === 'marketplace'`. I verified the writers of `source`: install-local writes `'marketplace'` at install (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1951`) and at rehydrate (`:1022`); `ObjectQL.registerApp` defaults `'code'` (`engine.ts:8782`) for the host stack, each member of an artifact's `packages[]` and every plugin manifest; `'authored'` is written only by `registry.installPackage(manifest, 'authored', ...)` from `protocol-package-install.ts:310`, `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:1697` and the `sys_packages` hydration (`service-package/src/index.ts:777`). The control-plane install (`POST /api/v1/cloud-connection/install`) only proxies to the cloud and registers nothing locally, so install-local is the only local door that writes `'marketplace'`. That half of the classification is sound.
- The other half is not: the stamp the classification reads, and the source the artifact entry may state, are both written by the installed package itself. Two reachable downgrades to the host's root, each through the card's own door, `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` with an inline manifest, by reading (not measured, read-only shape):
  - **(M1) A self-stamped `_packageId`.** `ConnectorBaseSchema` spreads `MetadataProtectionFields` (`connector.zod.ts:1055-1081`), so `_packageId` is a declared, optional key on a `connectors[]` entry and survives any parse. The managed install path registers the body as received (`normalizeBundle(inlineManifest)` → `convertPackageBodyForward` → `manifestService.register(converted, { source: 'marketplace' })` → `registerApp`); the collection loop registers each connector with `stampPackage(toRegister, ownerId, ownerVersion)` then `registerItem(..., ownerId)` (`engine.ts:9135`), and both stamp through `applyProtection`, which writes `_packageId` only while it is `undefined` (`protection.zod.ts:237`). Nothing refuses a body stamp that disagrees with `ownerId` for a connector (the ADR-0086 D3 refusal beside it covers `permissions` only). So an installed entry carrying `_packageId: 'com.host.showcase'` (a `'code'` row) or `_packageId: 'nobody'` (no row) is classified as the host's and handed `createPackageFileLoader(this.options.packageRoot)`: the measured cross-package read, one key away. The unit control "a stamp no row answers is the host's" pins the fail-open the spoof uses.
  - **(M2) An artifact entry stating `source: 'code'`.** install-local admits a body with `packages[]` (it reads `manifest.packages` itself at `:1667-1670`); the `manifest` service resolves entries through `resolveArtifactPackageEntries`, which keeps each entry's own `source` (`artifact-packages.ts:358`, `ArtifactPackageSourceSchema` admits `'code'` and `'marketplace'`, `stack.zod.ts:2010`), and registers with `source ?? options?.source` (`objectql/src/plugin.ts:944`): the entry's word wins over the door's `'marketplace'`. An installed bundle whose member states `source: 'code'` lands a `'code'` row, and every connector it declares reads the host's root. The spec's docblock reserves that statement for a control plane merging installs into the boot artifact; the install-local door does not withhold it.
- Fail-open on no registry / no row: no registry means no door could have written a row, which the code justifies. "A stamp no row answers = host" is the composed stack's residual owner (ADR-0130 D4) and is a real host case, but it is also what M1 exploits; it cannot stay a bare default once the stamp is the package's own word.
- Both members: `ConnectorProviderContext` has exactly two package-anchored members (`loadPackageFile`, `resolvePackagePath`); the built-in `openapi` factory dereferences only the first (`openapi-provider.ts:204`), `mcp` only the second (`mcp-provider.ts:351-352`), and neither reads `process.cwd()` itself; the only `process.cwd()` default is inside `resolveInsidePackageRoot` (`plugin.ts:315`), which an installed entry no longer reaches. `mcp-connector.ts:225` passes `transport.cwd` through, and `providerConfig.transport` carries no author-written `cwd` (the provider's own docblock). No third road found.
- Reconcile timing: `installPackage` writes the row before the collection loop registers any item (`registry.ts:6919-6931`, then `registerApp` step 2+), and `announceHotInstall` triggers `metadata:reloaded` with `{ changed: [...] }` only (`:3942`), so `captureReloadedConnectors` keeps no unstamped payload that could shadow the registry's stamped items. The materializer reads the registry object once per run but calls `getPackage` per entry, so the row is live. No ordering hole.
- Q1 (`'authored'`): reachable today, outside this card's ruling. `metadata-type-schemas.ts:272` binds `connector` to `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`, which carries `provider` / `providerConfig`, so a stored row with `providerConfig.spec: './x.json'` is storable through the metadata door; the post-boot reconcile reads stored rows through `readMetaItemsFromProtocol`, which stamps each with its `package_id` (`protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts:165`, an `'authored'` row or none) and both fall to the host's root. Also reachable with no package at all (an environment-authored connector), which is the same class on a hosted tenant. A finding to file, not a must-fix for this head.
- Q2 (every stdio `mcp` entry of an installed package refused): acceptable. The factory asks `resolvePackagePath('.')` unconditionally and the only alternative, no member at all, inherits the host's working directory (the measured reach by another road); the refusal and the docs name `http` as the road. Route B is not foreclosed.
- Message: the refusal is thrown before any resolution and interpolates only the entry name, the declaring package id and the author's own ref; no host absolute path can appear (pinned by `not.toContain(path.resolve(fixtureRoot))` in both unit cases). The `openapi` wrapper adds only its own prose. The cloud seat's finding 3 on #27293 holds here.
- Tests: the 6 unit cases and the 4 dogfood cases pin what the PR claims, including the host controls; the ablation the dev reports turns exactly the installed cases red. Nothing pins M1 or M2 because nothing in the design refuses them.
- Docs row and changeset: accurate for the mechanism as built (door names, `source: 'marketplace'`, `os build` remedy, `http` for MCP, host entries unchanged). The sentence "never resolved against the host's directory" overstates until M1 and M2 close.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-automation` patch, as declared. Behaviour narrows for one class of entry (an installed package's package-relative refs, and every stdio `mcp` entry of an installed package); no published schema or `packages/spec` member changes; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Boundary change: what an installed package's connector entry may read or launch on the host. The intended boundary (declaring package's root, never the host's) matches the contract text. The boundary as built is keyed on two inputs the installed package writes itself (M1, M2), so the installed package can opt out of it.
- Fail-open defaults: no registry (justified), a stamp with no row (unsafe while the stamp is the package's own).
- A hosted tenant never sees a host path in the refusal (verified).
- No `packages/spec` change; the claim's file surface is respected. Both remedies below sit outside `service-automation`; the claim says stop and report on that, so the seat widens the claim or routes them, rather than the dev deciding alone.

### ④ Design judgment

The change holds against the scenario it was accepted on (an honest installed manifest naming a host file or location) and against the contract's words. It does not hold against the adversary the card names ("an installed package must not be able to bind another package's files by guessing a path"), because the classification trusts the package's own `_packageId` and its own artifact-entry `source`. Must-fix and should-fix, one line each:

- **must-fix M1**: a connector (any collection item) registered under `ownerId` must not keep a body-carried `_packageId` that differs from `ownerId`: overwrite it, or refuse it the way `permissionSetOwnerRegistrationRefusal` refuses a permission set (`engine.ts:9120-9135`), and pin with an installed entry stamped `_packageId` of a `'code'` package being refused its ref.
- **must-fix M2**: an install-local install must register every `packages[]` member as `'marketplace'` whatever the entry states (refuse or override `source: 'code'` at the install-local door or make the door's `options.source` win in `objectql/src/plugin.ts:944` when the door states one), and pin it with a two-member inline bundle whose member states `source: 'code'`.
- **should-fix S1**: drop the bare "a stamp no row answers is the host's" default: answer host only for the residual owner id the artifact names (or no stamp), refuse every other stamp no row answers, and retitle the unit control accordingly.
- **should-fix S2**: file Q1 as a finding (class b): a stored or `'authored'` provider-bound connector row reads the host's root through the same two members, reachable through the metadata door bound to `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`.
- **should-fix S3**: the `installedDeclaringPackageOf` docblock should state what it trusts (the registering door's row) and what it does not (the item's stamp, the entry's stated source) once M1 and M2 make that true.
- **should-fix S4**: the dev's out-of-scope restart finding (installed connectors absent from `GET /automation/connectors` after rehydrate, inline entry included) is a real class a defect in a sibling lane; file it so it is not lost in a report comment.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-28534-installed-package-file-ref`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcVBKAFk1ntXSjvPt7U`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
